chapter: Compositions, singers and the end of the big band
title: Driving the Caddy and the bus driver who taught him
summary: He likes to drive, and recalls driver Ed Fitzgerald on the Dallas dash.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, according to some of the stories I've read, you don't mind flying your Caddy on the road though. [Laughter]
No. I get on pretty good. If I got time to make it, and I've got to go, I'll get in the Caddy. If I don't have that much time, then whatever need, I'll do.

I used to, in the bus, when we was travelling for one night stands. I used to get in my car instead of riding the bus, and follow the bus, you know, until we'd get there. Now, I don't need that car there.
But, I didn't mind driving. I just wanted it when I needed the car to go somewhere. I didn't want to take the bus or this and that. You know?

So, the bus driver used to say just make 50 miles an hour steady. And I was out there doing 60 and 70 and I told myself I was gonna get there in time before the band got there? And you, and when I had to stop for a light and he was doing 50 miles, he was behind me. He taught me how to drive on the road. His name was Fitzgerald. I'll never forget it. Ed Fitzgerald, an Irishman. He was beautiful. A senior citizen. He drove me all the way from Texas to New York. I don't know how he did it. Three thousand miles.
That's when I was telling you about the Savoy Ballroom when the Golden Gate was opening up. He was the driver. I'll never forget him. But, he got us there for us to get on that band stand in time.
I was really waiting for this tape to end. But, we have a little bit more there.
You've got a little more tape?
